title: The gap step's ledger guard counts every error check.py gives the ledger, not only path:line citations
goal: ql_apply.gap_one rejects a gap entry and restores the ledger when check.py would refuse it for any reason the quoted question carries (a topic: mark naming no article, a [DOC S99999] or [DECISION x] tag), not only a path:line citation (ledger_citation_errors), so no short logged question can wedge apply --push again

gates.question: The suite is at the 100-id ceiling and the item's check selects a test by -k apply_gap_guard_all_check_errors: which test carries that name?
options: Rename the existing gap-step test and extend it
Add a new test id and ask the operator to raise the ceiling
gates.recommendation: Rename the existing gap-step test and extend it
gates.answer: Rename the existing gap-step test and extend it

notes: Planned at the 2026-10-12 draft triage (sprint 3 of 19, "Checks that passed broken work: ledger citations, lint paths, the held-out reword gate and the query-log apply guards"): it fixes a failure that recurred in recent sprints and blocks the EP-gzr4mmkm fitness test that a content sprint lands on headless Sonnet workers with no operator step beyond its gates. Premise: ql_apply.gap_one for a question holding 'topic: no/such-topic' returns state applied, and the _gaps.md entry holds a topic mark check.py refuses as an unknown topic (script run at planning 2026-10-12: state applied). Gate.ledger_errors calls only check.ledger_citation_errors; check.py is in touches because the other ledger checks live in check.main. Order: after BG-676tplds and BG-bbcc5f4s (shared check.py, ql_apply.py, test_redact.py).
